summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Yuanying studied under Dagong, Miaolian, Zeng Xi, Tongzhi, Bazhi Toutuo, and Yekai. He served as abbot at Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan Temples, and held leadership roles in the Buddhist Association of China.

Yudru Tsomu works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University, where she was supervised by Leonard van der Kuijp and advised by Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn.

Yuen Ren Chao was a linguistics and Sinology scholar who studied at Cornell, Harvard, and Tsinghua Universities. He held positions at Cornell (~1919–1920), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua University (~1925–1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He founded Huayan University, where he also served as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Bsam gtan, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1965 to 1974. He later served as president (学長) of Taisho University from circa 2010 to 2013.
Yui Chi Lau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ying-Kuang Chu and founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society.

Yui Suzuki works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She studied at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna, and held posts at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University (1988–1997), and Soka University.

Yuichi Shionoya was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Hitotsubashi University (~1950–1953) and Nagoya University (~1954–1958). He later held an academic post at Nagoya University from circa 1964 to 1971.

Yuishin Ito was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Bukkyo and Doshisha Universities. He held teaching posts and professor emeritus status at Bukkyo University, served as head of Kyoto Bunkyo Gakuen, and held temple posts.

Yujiro Motora was a scholar of philosophy who studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo from circa 1888 to 1912 and at the Tokyo University of Education.

Yujun Endo worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Taisho University as an associate professor (attested 1991) and professor emeritus (attested 2014), and served as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani works in the field of Buddhist studies. She has held posts as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (both attested 2015).

Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies under Kenyu Mitomo and is attested in 2026 at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University holding a doctorate.

Yukei Matsunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Koyasan, Tohoku, and Kyushu Universities. He served as director at Koyasan University in 1983 and also held a post at Shuchiin University.

Yuki Kyogoku works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. A doctoral student at the University of Leipzig (attested 2026), Kyogoku previously worked as an associate engineer at Accenture (2013–2014) and a research associate at Leipzig (2018).

Yuki Sasaki works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Sasaki held posts as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Yuki Shibuya works in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Shibuya was a project research fellow at the University of Tokyo in 2014 and earned a PhD there (2016–2018).
Yuki Takatsukasa specializes in Buddhist studies. Takatsukasa pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).
